record.title: Exact threshold conjecture for adding three-paths
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $t$ be a positive integer. Write $G\cup tP_3$ for the disjoint union of $G$ and $t$ copies of $P_3$, and let $\tau(G)$ be the maximum integer such that $G\cup sP_3$ is antimagic for every integer $s\leqslant\tau(G)$. **Exact threshold conjecture.** $G\cup tP_3$ is antimagic if and only if $t\leqslant\tau(G)$. Equivalently, $\tau(G)$ is the maximum integer $t$ such that $G\cup tP_3$ is antimagic. The source presents this as a conjectural strengthening of its upper bounds; it would settle the remaining cases in which the established bound $\beta(G)$ may exceed $\tau(G)$.
record.source_name: Angel Chavez, Parker Le, Derek Lin, Daphne Der-Fen Liu and Mason Shurman, “Antimagic Labeling for Unions of Graphs with Many Three-Paths”, arXiv:2203.14842 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.14842

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: The minimal-intensity conjecture for finite-time Euler singularities
record.statement:
Let $T_*<\infty$ and let $\omega\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^3\times[0,T_*))$ be a smooth solution of the 3D Euler equation that becomes singular as $t\to T_*$. **Minimal-intensity conjecture.** There exists a universal finite exponent $p_*$ such that

$$
\sup_{t\in[0,T_*)}\|\omega(t)\|_{L^{p_*}}=+\infty.
$$

The conjecture would show that every finite-time singularity has a universal minimum intensity in an $L^{p_*}$ norm, potentially without resolving the full blow-up problem.
record.source_name: Theodore D. Drivas and Tarek M. Elgindi, “Singularity formation in the incompressible Euler equation in finite and infinite time”, arXiv:2203.17221 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.17221

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: Nonlinear stability conjecture for N-spot ring patterns
record.statement:
Let an $N$-spot ring pattern have spot-spot distance equal to a stable zero $d_c$ of the interaction function $f$, so that $f(d_c)=0$ and $f'(d_c)>0$. The distance $d_c$ is called a binding radius, and the smallest such distance is the smallest binding distance. The $N$ zero eigenvalues associated with neutral modes are excluded from consideration.

**Nonlinear stability conjecture.** All $N$-spot ring patterns are nonlinearly stable unless the spot-spot distance is the smallest binding distance.

The preceding linear analysis gives eigenvalues with non-positive real parts after excluding the neutral modes; the conjecture concerns the effects of higher-order terms and asserts nonlinear stability for every binding radius except the smallest one.
record.source_name: Yasumasa Nishiura and Shuangquan Xie, “Dynamics of N-spot rings with oscillatory tails in a three-component reaction-diffusion system”, arXiv:2204.02740 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02740

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Generic bounded-complexity conjecture for dispersing billiard tables
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite horizon dispersing billiard map, and let $K_n$ be the maximum number of curves in ${\mathcal{S}}_n$ that intersect at one point. The sequence of complexities is **bounded** if there exists $K>0$ such that

$$
K_n \leq K \quad \text{for all } n \in \mathbb{Z}.
$$

**Bounded-complexity conjecture.** For typical finite horizon dispersing billiard configurations, the sequence of complexities $K_n$ is bounded.

The known general estimate is only linear, namely $K_n\leq K|n|$ for some $K>0$. The conjecture is refuted when the table has a periodic orbit with a grazing collision, although the sparse recurrence condition may still hold in that case.
record.source_name: Mark F. Demers and Alexey Korepanov, “Rates of mixing for the measure of maximal entropy of dispersing billiard maps”, arXiv:2204.04684 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.04684

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2022). “Notice that the conjecture does not hold if the table has a periodic orbit with a grazing collision; however can still hold in this case, and does in all known examples (see ).”

record.title: Rudin–Shapiro maximum conjecture below powers of two
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{r}$ denote the Rudin–Shapiro sequence, and let $A_{\mathbf{r}}(d)$ be its associated arithmetic-progression counting function.

**Rudin–Shapiro maximum conjecture.** For all integers $k \geq 5$,

$$
\max_{1 \leq d \leq 2^k-2} A_{\mathbf{r}}(d) \leq 2^{k-1}
$$

and

$$
A_{\mathbf{r}}(2^k-1)=
\begin{cases}
2^{k-1}+1, & \text{if } k \equiv 0 \pmod{2},\\
2^{k-1}+3, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

This is presented as a consequence that would follow from the Rudin–Shapiro bound conjecture together with a theorem, so its resolution is tied to those preceding results.
record.source_name: Bartosz Sobolewski, “On monochromatic arithmetic progressions in binary words associated with pattern sequences”, arXiv:2204.05287 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.05287

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: The Dirac--Goodman--Pollack conjecture for pseudolines
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal L$ be a nontrivial arrangement of $n$ pseudolines, and let $r(\mathcal L)$ be the maximum number of crossing points, or vertices of the arrangement, lying on a pseudoline in $\mathcal L$.

**Dirac--Goodman--Pollack conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
r(\mathcal L) \geq c n.
$$

This is the pseudoline-arrangement formulation of the Dirac problem and is also described in terms of allowable sequences. In the abstract, the paper states that the conjecture is confirmed with the concrete bound $c=1/845$.
record.source_name: Adrian Dumitrescu, “The Dirac–Goodman–Pollack Conjecture”, arXiv:2204.06101 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.06101

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2022). “An infinite family of counterexamples to the strong Dirac conjecture was found by Felsner .”

record.title: Gerbner–Palmer's conjecture that paths are Turán-good
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a graph with chromatic number $\chi(F)=k+1$. A graph $H$ is **$F$-Turán-good** if, for all sufficiently large $n$, the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph equals the number of copies of $H$ in the Turán graph $T(n,k)$.

**Gerbner–Palmer's conjecture.** Every path is $K_{k+1}$-Turán-good for every $k$.

The conjecture asks when the Turán graph is extremal for generalized Turán problems. In this paper, the authors state that they prove the claim for paths, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Dániel Gerbner, “Paths are Turán-good”, arXiv:2204.07638 (2022).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2112.14895](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.14895), [arXiv:2102.01332](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.01332).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.07638

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Stability conjecture for exterior Fraser-Sargent surfaces
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $l$ be relatively prime integers with $k>l>0$, and let $EFS_{k,l}$ be the exterior Fraser-Sargent surface in $\mathbb E^4\setminus\mathring{\mathbb B}^4$ associated with these parameters. Its index is denoted by $\operatorname{Ind}(EFS_{k,l})$. **Stability conjecture.** For all such $k,l$,

$$
\operatorname{Ind}(EFS_{k,l})=0,
$$

so every surface $EFS_{k,l}$ is stable. The authors explain that they were unable to compute the index rigorously; the conjecture is supported by a computer-assisted argument and remains open.
record.source_name: Vladimir Medvedev and Egor Morozov, “On the Index of Fraser-Sargent-type minimal surfaces”, arXiv:2204.07972 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.07972

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Jakobson–Naud's half-plane conjecture for zeros of the Selberg zeta function
record.statement:
Let $Z_X(s)$ be the Selberg zeta function of the symmetric infinite-area hyperbolic surface under consideration, and let $b4$ denote the exponent of convergence of its limit set. 

**Jakobson–Naud's conjecture.** There are only finitely many zeros in the half-plane

$$
\Re(s)>\frac{\delta}{2}
$$

and this is the largest half-plane with this property: for every $\varepsilon>0$, there are infinitely many zeros in the half-plane

$$
\Re(s)>\frac{\delta}{2}-\varepsilon.
$$

The conjecture identifies the boundary $\Re(s)=\delta/2$ as the sharp finiteness threshold for zeros of the Selberg zeta function. It is attributed to Jakobson and Naud and is presented here as an open conjecture.
record.source_name: Mark Pollicott and Polina Vytnova, “Zeros of the Selberg zeta function for symmetric infinite area hyperbolic surfaces”, arXiv:2204.08218 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.08218

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Booksize lower-bound conjecture for graphs with large spectral radius
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, and let $bk(G)$ denote its booksize, the maximum number of triangles sharing a common edge.

**Booksize lower-bound conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda(G)\geq \sqrt{m},
$$

then, unless $G$ is a complete bipartite graph, there is a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
bk(G)\geq c\sqrt{m}.
$$

Nikiforov's cited result gives the weaker lower bound $bk(G)>\frac{1}{12}\sqrt[4]{m}$ under the same spectral-radius hypothesis, so the proposed order-$\sqrt m$ bound remains open.
record.source_name: Yongtao Li and Yuejian Peng, “The maximum spectral radius of non-bipartite graphs forbidding short odd cycles”, arXiv:2204.09884 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.09884

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Thomason's balanced clique-subdivision conjecture
record.statement:
A **balanced subdivision** of a graph $H$ is obtained by replacing every edge of $H$ with an internally vertex-disjoint path of the same length; write this as $TH^{(\ell)}$ when that length is $\ell$. For a graph $G$, let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. **Thomason's conjecture.** For every $k\ge 1$, there exists a function $f(k)$ such that if

$$
\delta(G)\ge f(k),
$$

then $G$ contains a balanced subdivision of $K_k$. This conjecture was confirmed by Liu and Montgomery, so the assertion is now a theorem; the paper studies stronger quantitative results for balanced clique subdivisions.
record.source_name: Bingyu Luan, Yantao Tang, Guanghui Wang and Donglei Yang, “Balanced subdivisions of cliques in graphs”, arXiv:2204.12012 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.12012

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Thomason's conjecture on balanced subdivisions
record.statement:
Given a graph $H$ and an integer $\ell$, a **balanced $H$-subdivision** is obtained by replacing every edge of $H$ with an internally vertex-disjoint path of length $\ell$, denoted $TH^{(\ell)}$. For a graph $G$, let $\delta(G)$ be its minimum degree. **Thomason's conjecture.** For every $k\ge 1$, there exists a function $f(k)$ such that if

$$
\delta(G)\ge f(k),
$$

then $G$ contains a balanced subdivision of $K_k$. The source states that Liu and Montgomery confirmed this conjecture. The result is part of the study of how minimum or average degree forces subdivisions with all replacement paths of equal length.
record.source_name: Bingyu Luan, Yantao Tang, Guanghui Wang and Donglei Yang, “Balanced subdivisions of cliques in graphs”, arXiv:2204.12012 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.12012

record.title: Mixed Granville–Soundararajan conjecture for twisted character sums
record.statement:
Let $\chi$ be a non-principal character modulo $q$, let $1\leqslant x\leqslant\min\{q,T\}$, and let $2T\leqslant t\leqslant5T$. Write $\chi_0$ for the principal character modulo $q$, and let $P^{+}(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. 

**Mixed conjecture.** There exists a constant $A>0$ such that, uniformly in these ranges, 

$$
\sum_{n\leqslant x}\frac{\chi(n)}{n^{it}}=\sum_{\substack{n\leqslant x\\P^{+}(n)\leqslant y}}\frac{\chi(n)}{n^{it}}+o\bigl(\Psi(x,y;\chi_0)\bigr),\qquad\text{as }q\to\infty,\ T\to\infty,
$$

where $y=(\log(qT)+\log^2x)(\log_2(qT))^A$.

This combines the character-sum and oscillatory smooth-approximation conjectures. The source gives no evidence of a proof or disproof.
record.source_name: Daodao Yang, “Extreme values of derivatives of zeta and L-functions”, arXiv:2204.13826 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13826

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: The prime-tuple hypothesis for simultaneous primality of linear forms
record.statement:
Let $(a_i)$ and $(b_i)$ be finite collections of integers with $a_i\neq 0$ for every $i$. The linear forms are subject to a **congruence obstruction** if there is a prime $p$ such that, for every integer $x$, at least one of the values $a_i x+b_i$ is divisible by $p$.

**Prime-tuple hypothesis.** If no congruence obstruction exists, then there are infinitely many values of $x$ such that every $a_i x+b_i$ is prime.

This hypothesis is generally believed to be true, but is far beyond current methods; it is used in the paper to construct additive and difference decompositions of the signed primes.
record.source_name: Imre Z. Ruzsa, “Additive decomposition of signed prime”, arXiv:2204.14013 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.14013

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Connected size Ramsey number conjecture for matchings versus $C_4$
record.statement:
Let $nK_2$ be a matching with $n$ edges, and let $C_4$ be the cycle on four vertices. For graphs $G$, write $G\to (nK_2,C_4)$ when every red-blue edge-colouring of $G$ contains either a red copy of $nK_2$ or a blue copy of $C_4$, and let $\hat r_c(nK_2,C_4)$ denote the minimum number of edges in a connected graph $G$ with this property.

**Connected size Ramsey conjecture.** For all positive integers $n$,

$$
\hat r_c(nK_2,C_4)=\left\lfloor\frac{9n-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The paper proves the matching upper bound for every positive integer $n$ by constructing connected graphs with the stated number of edges. The conjecture asserts that this upper bound is tight for all $n$.
record.source_name: Sha Wang, Ruyu Song, Yixin Zhang and Yanbo Zhang, “Connected size Ramsey numbers of matchings versus a small path or cycle”, arXiv:2205.03965 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03965

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Seven-colour conjecture for odd colouring of toroidal graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph that embeds in the torus. A **proper odd vertex-colouring** of $G$ is a proper colouring in which, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some colour appears an odd number of times in the neighbourhood $N(v)$. Let $\chi_o(G)$ denote the smallest number of colours in a proper odd vertex-colouring of $G$.

**Seven-colour conjecture for toroidal graphs.** Every toroidal graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi_o(G) \leq 7.
$$

The paper proves the bounds $7 \leq \chi_o(T) \leq 9$ for the torus $T$, so the conjecture would determine the exact value $\chi_o(T)=7$. It remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Harry Metrebian, “Odd colouring on the torus”, arXiv:2205.04398 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.04398

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Second-largest eigenvalue conjecture for balanced complete-graph configurations
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$, and let $p:[n]\to{\mathbb R}^d$ satisfy $\|p(i)\|=1$ for every $i\in[n]$ and

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n p(i)=0.
$$

Assume that the image of $p$ has size at least $3$. **Second-largest eigenvalue conjecture.** The second largest eigenvalue of $L(K_n,p)$ is $n/2$, and its multiplicity is exactly $n-1$. This conjecture concerns the spectrum of the Laplacian associated with balanced point configurations; the preceding argument establishes that $n/2$ has multiplicity at least $n-1$, while the asserted second-largest-eigenvalue and exact-multiplicity statement remains open.
record.source_name: Alan Lew, Eran Nevo, Yuval Peled and Orit E. Raz, “On the d-dimensional algebraic connectivity of graphs”, arXiv:2205.05530 (2022).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2006.12994](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.12994), [arXiv:1706.01933](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.01933), [arXiv:0804.1285](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.1285).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05530

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Large-eigenvalue sum conjecture for complete-graph Laplacians
record.statement:
Let $p:[n]\to{\mathbb R}^d$ be injective. **Large-eigenvalue sum conjecture.** The sum of the $n$ largest eigenvalues of $L(K_n,p)$ is at least

$$
\frac{n(n+1)}{2}.
$$

The conjecture improves the previously established lower bound for this eigenvalue sum. Since the largest eigenvalue is $n$ for every non-constant $p$, it is equivalently a lower bound of $n/2$ for the average of the next $n-1$ largest eigenvalues; it remains open.
record.source_name: Alan Lew, Eran Nevo, Yuval Peled and Orit E. Raz, “On the d-dimensional algebraic connectivity of graphs”, arXiv:2205.05530 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05530

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Strong enumeration conjecture for q-ary codes
record.statement:
Fix an integer $q\ge 2$. A $q$-ary code of length $n$ and distance $d$ is a subset of $[q]^n$ whose elements are pairwise separated by Hamming distance at least $d$, and let $A_q(n,d)$ denote the maximum size of such a code. **Strong enumeration conjecture for q-ary codes.** For every fixed $c>0$, the number of $q$-ary codes of length $n$ and distance $d$ is

$$
2^{O(A_q(n,d))}
$$

whenever

$$
d<(1-q^{-1}-c)n.
$$

The conjecture would give a substantially stronger enumeration bound than the paper's proved results. Its main obstacle is the apparent lack of strong supersaturation estimates showing that sets much larger than $A_q(n,d)$ contain many pairs at distance at most $d$; the source presents it as likely quite difficult and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Dingding Dong, Nitya Mani and Yufei Zhao, “On the number of error correcting codes”, arXiv:2205.12363 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.12363

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Kleitman–Winston conjecture on enumerating H-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a fixed bipartite graph that contains a cycle, and let $\operatorname{ex}(n,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $H$. **Kleitman–Winston's conjecture.** For every such graph $H$, the number of $H$-free graphs on $n$ labeled vertices is

$$
2^{O_H(\operatorname{ex}(n,H))}.
$$

The paper cites this as an analogous conjecture motivating the stronger code-enumeration conjecture; no resolution is supplied in the source, so it is recorded as open here.
record.source_name: Dingding Dong, Nitya Mani and Yufei Zhao, “On the number of error correcting codes”, arXiv:2205.12363 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1801.04584](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04584).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.12363

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Polynomial-time Maximum Independent Set in graphs with bounded induced cycle packing
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let an **$\mathcal{O}_k$-free graph** be a graph containing no induced subgraph from the family $\mathcal{O}_k$.

**Polynomial-time independent-set conjecture.** $\textsc{Maximum Independent Set}$ is solvable in polynomial time in $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs.

The conjecture would extend the known polynomial-time result for graphs of bounded odd cycle packing. The paper proves it in the sparse case and gives a quasi-polynomial-time algorithm in general, but does not establish polynomial-time solvability for arbitrary $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Édouard Bonnet, Hugues Déprés, Louis Esperet, Colin Geniet, Claire Hilaire, Stéphan Thomassé and Alexandra Wesolek, “Sparse graphs with bounded induced cycle packing number have logarithmic treewidth”, arXiv:2206.00594 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00594

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2022). “For $k=2$, when no complete bipartite is excluded as a subgraph, Le conjectured the following, which had been raised as an open question earlier by Raymond .”

record.title: The Erdős–Tuza–Valtr cap-cup conjecture
record.statement:
Let an $a$-cap be a set of $a$ points lying on the graph of a downwardly convex function, and let a $b$-cup be a set of $b$ points lying on the graph of an upwardly convex function. Call $(n,a,b)$ a **triplet** when $2\leq a,b\leq n\leq a+b-2$. Let $N(n,a,b)$ be the maximum size of a general-position point set in the plane containing no $n$-gon, $a$-cap, or $b$-cup.

**Erdős–Tuza–Valtr conjecture.** For every triplet $(n,a,b)$,

$$
N(n,a,b)=\sum_{i=n-b}^{a-2}\binom{n-2}{i}.
$$

This strengthens the Erdős–Szekeres problem by simultaneously forbidding convex $n$-gons, caps, and cups. The source states that Erdős, Tuza, and Valtr showed this generalization is equivalent to the Erdős–Szekeres conjecture; its status therefore follows the unresolved status of that conjecture.
record.source_name: Jineon Baek, “On the Erdős-Tuza-Valtr Conjecture”, arXiv:2206.04260 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04260

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The set-theoretic Erdős–Szekeres conjecture for weak polygons
record.statement:
A configuration consists of a linearly ordered vertex set together with designated 3-caps and 3-cups. A **weak $(a,b)$-gon** is a pair of an $a$-cap and a $b$-cup sharing the same endpoints; a weak $n$-gon is a weak $(a,b)$-gon with $a+b=n+2$. A configuration is weak $n$-gon free if it contains no weak $n$-gon. Let $\widehat{N}(n)$ be the maximum size of a weak $n$-gon free configuration.

**Set-theoretic Erdős–Szekeres conjecture.** For every $n\geq 2$,

$$
\widehat{N}(n)=2^{n-2}.
$$

This is a combinatorial generalization of the Erdős–Szekeres conjecture. The source contrasts it with the corresponding strong-polygon formulation, for which counterexamples are known for $n=7$ and $8$; the weak-polygon conjecture itself is presented as an open proposal.
record.source_name: Jineon Baek, “On the Erdős-Tuza-Valtr Conjecture”, arXiv:2206.04260 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04260

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The set-theoretic Erdős–Tuza–Valtr conjecture
record.statement:
Call $(n,a,b)$ a triplet when $2\leq a,b\leq n\leq a+b-2$. In a configuration, a weak $n$-gon is a pair of an $a$-cap and a $b$-cup sharing endpoints with $a+b=n+2$. Let $\widehat{N}(n,a,b)$ be the maximum size of a configuration containing no weak $n$-gon, no $a$-cap, and no $b$-cup.

**Set-theoretic Erdős–Tuza–Valtr conjecture.** For every triplet $(n,a,b)$,

$$
\widehat{N}(n,a,b)=\sum_{i=n+2-b}^{a}\binom{n-2}{i-2}.
$$

This is the configuration-theoretic analogue of the Erdős–Tuza–Valtr conjecture, extending the weak-polygon version of the Erdős–Szekeres problem. The source presents it as a conjectural generalization, with no resolution supplied.
record.source_name: Jineon Baek, “On the Erdős-Tuza-Valtr Conjecture”, arXiv:2206.04260 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04260

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: Kiselev–Kupavskii–Patkós minimum-degree conjecture for union antichains
record.statement:
Let $\mathscr{P}([n])$ be the power set of $[n]$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathscr{P}([n])$ is a **$(2\ell+1)$-union antichain** if it is an antichain and $\lvert F\cup F'\rvert\leq 2\ell+1$ for every $F,F'\in\mathcal{F}$. Write $\delta(\mathcal{F})$ for its minimum degree. 

**Kiselev–Kupavskii–Patkós' conjecture.** If $1\leq 2\ell+1<n$ and $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\mathscr{P}([n])$ is a $(2\ell+1)$-union antichain, then

$$
\delta(\mathcal{F})\leq\binom{n-1}{\ell-1}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the minimum degree of union antichains and is equivalent to their conjecture on the diversity of an intersecting antichain. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Marcelo Sales and Bjarne Schülke, “A local version of Katona's intersection theorem”, arXiv:2206.04278 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04278

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: The polylogarithmic conjecture for edge-ordered forests
record.statement:
An **edge-ordered graph** is a finite simple graph equipped with a linear order on its edges; its extremal function ${\mathrm{ex}}_<(n,H)$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex edge-ordered graph avoiding $H$. **Edge-ordered forest conjecture.** For every edge-ordered forest $H$ of order chromatic number $2$,

$$
{\mathrm{ex}}_<(n,H)=n\log^{O(1)}n.
$$

The paper proves the weaker bound ${\mathrm{ex}}_<(n,H)=n2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$, so improving it to a polylogarithmic factor is the main open problem identified by the authors.
record.source_name: Gaurav Kucheriya and Gábor Tardos, “A characterization of edge-ordered graphs with almost linear extremal functions”, arXiv:2206.12979 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12979

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2022). “Many special cases of this conjecture have been established, but it remains open in its full generality.”

record.title: Hypergraph Hadwiger conjecture for the chromatic number
record.statement:
For an integer $t\geq 2$, let $h(t)$ be the largest chromatic number of a hypergraph with no $K_t$-minor; the paper establishes that this quantity exists. A hypergraph is **$K_t$-minor-free** if it does not contain $K_t$ as a minor, where hypergraph minors are obtained by deleting vertices or hyperedges and contracting hyperedges. **Hypergraph Hadwiger conjecture.** For every integer $t\geq 2$,

$$
h(t)=\left\lceil\frac{3}{2}(t-1)\right\rceil.
$$

Equivalently, every $K_t$-minor-free hypergraph $H$ satisfies

$$
\chi(H)\leq\left\lceil\frac{3}{2}(t-1)\right\rceil.
$$

The lower bound is attained by complete $3$-uniform hypergraphs, so the conjecture would give the exact extremal chromatic number. The conjecture remains open even for $K_3$-minor-free hypergraphs.
record.source_name: Raphael Steiner, “Coloring hypergraphs with excluded minors”, arXiv:2206.13635 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.13635

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2022). “Hadwiger's conjecture, among the most famous open problems in graph theory, states that every graph that does not contain $K_t$ as a minor is properly $(t-1)$-colorable.”

record.title: Rationality and upper bound conjecture for adjacent AKLT edge projectors
record.statement:
Let $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$ be positive integers or half-integers. For adjacent edges $e=\{1,2\}$ and $e'=\{2,3\}$, let $P_{12}=P_{S_1+S_2}(\vec{S}_1+\vec{S}_2)$ and $P_{23}=P_{S_2+S_3}(\vec{S}_2+\vec{S}_3)$, and denote by $s(P_{12}P_{23})$ the largest singular value of $P_{12}P_{23}$ that is not equal to $1$. **Rationality and upper bound conjecture.** The quantity $s^2(P_{12}P_{23})$ is rational. If $S_1,S_3\leq S_2$, then

$$
s^2(P_{12}P_{23})\leq \frac{1}{4},
$$

with equality if and only if $S_1=S_2=S_3$. This conjecture concerns the local projector overlaps governing sample-complexity bounds for verification of Affleck–Kennedy–Lieb–Tasaki states. The source notes that the explicit values for spins at most $5/2$ suggest the claim; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Tianyi Chen, Yunting Li and Huangjun Zhu, “Efficient verification of Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki states”, arXiv:2206.15307 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15307

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: Dujmović–Morin conjecture on the number of graphs with bounded obstacle number
record.statement:
Given a graph $G$, let its obstacle number be the minimum number of faces in a straight-line drawing whose union intersects every non-edge, and let $f(h,n)$ denote the number of $n$-vertex graphs with obstacle number at most $h$. For positive integers $n$ and $h$, the conjecture is

$$
f(h,n)\in 2^{g(n)\cdot o(h)},
$$

where $g(n)\in O(n\log^2 n)$. **Dujmović–Morin conjecture.** For all positive integers $n$ and $h$, we have $f(h,n)\in 2^{g(n)\cdot o(h)}$, where $g(n)\in O(n\log^2 n)$. This conjecture concerns the growth of the number of graphs admitting drawings with bounded obstacle number, and would constrain how many graphs can have small obstacle number. The cited context gives lower bounds on the maximum obstacle number, but does not state that this conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Martin Balko, Steven Chaplick, Robert Ganian, Siddharth Gupta, Michael Hoffmann, Pavel Valtr and Alexander Wolff, “Bounding and computing obstacle numbers of graphs”, arXiv:2206.15414 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15414

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

record.title: Ahanjideh–Ekim–Yıldız conjecture for $Z(d)$
record.statement:
For odd $d$, let $Z(d)$ denote the maximum matching number of a factor-critical, almost regular, triangle-free graph of maximum degree $d$ in the class used by the paper. The paper establishes the value of $Z(d)$ for even $d$ and for $d\in\{3,5\}$, and gives bounds for the remaining odd values.

**$Z(d)$ conjecture.** For odd $d\geq 21$,

$$
Z(d)=\left\lfloor\frac{5(d+1)}{4}\right\rfloor.
$$

Determining $Z(d)$ is crucial for evaluating the proposed extremal formula and constructing the corresponding graphs. The conjecture is motivated by results suggesting that sufficiently dense triangle-free graphs are blow-ups of a $5$-cycle, but the stated range remains open in the paper.
record.source_name: Milad Ahanjideh, Tınaz Ekim and Mehmet Akif Yıldız, “Maximum size of a triangle-free graph with bounded maximum degree and matching number”, arXiv:2207.02271 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02271

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: The four-color bound for locally irregular edge colorings
record.statement:
A graph is **locally irregular** if the degrees of the end-vertices of every edge are distinct. An edge coloring is **locally irregular** if every color induces a locally irregular subgraph. A graph is **colorable** if it admits a locally irregular edge coloring. For a colorable graph $G$, let $\chi_{\rm irr}^{\prime}(G)$ be the smallest number of colors required by such a coloring. **The four-color bound.** Every colorable connected graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\chi_{\rm irr}^{\prime}(G)\leq 4.
$$

This weaker version of the Local Irregularity Conjecture is established for all colorable cacti, as stated in the paper’s context, so the candidate is treated as solved.
record.source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Local Irregularity Conjecture vs. cacti”, arXiv:2207.03941 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.03941

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The Erdős–Rogers Ramsey-number separation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\ell\geq 3$ be an integer. The Ramsey number $\mathbf{R}(t,m)$ is the minimum integer $n$ such that every graph on $n$ vertices contains either a clique $K_t$ or an independent set of size $m$. **The Ramsey-number separation conjecture.** There exist constants $c=c(\ell)>0$ and $N=N(\ell)>0$ such that, for every $m>N$, 

$$
\mathbf{R}(\ell-1,m)\leq \frac{\mathbf{R}(\ell,m)}{m^c}.
$$

This conjecture asserts a polynomial separation between consecutive diagonal Ramsey numbers and would provide quantitative information about the growth of Ramsey numbers for larger cliques, whose exact order of magnitude is not known for $t\geq 4$.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Ce Chen, Grace McCourt and Cassie Murley, “Ramsey-Turán Problems with small independence numbers”, arXiv:2207.10545 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.10545

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Shakan's conjecture on arbitrarily large improvements for sum-free subsets
record.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ be a set of size $n$. A subset of $A$ is **sum-free** if it contains no $x,y,z$ satisfying

$$
x+y=z.
$$

Let $s(A)$ denote the largest size of a sum-free subset of $A$.

**Shakan's conjecture.** For every positive integer $S$, there exists $N_S\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that

$$
s(A)\geq\frac{n+S}{3}
$$

for every $n\geq N_S$.

The question asks whether the standard lower bound for the largest sum-free subset can be improved by an arbitrarily large additive constant for sufficiently large sets. Bourgain proved a fixed improvement in broad circumstances, including the bound $s(A)\geq(n+2)/3$ for sets with coprime elements apart from $A=\{1,2\}$, but the asserted arbitrary improvement remains open.
record.source_name: George Shakan, “On the largest sum-free subset problem in the integers”, arXiv:2207.14210 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14210

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Shakan's stronger conjecture on the maximum of the sum-free Fourier function
record.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ be a set of size $n$, and let $S$ be a positive integer. Define

$$
f(x)=1_{[1/3,\,2/3)}-1/3,
$$

$$
f_A(x)=\sum_{a\in A}f(ax),
$$

and

$$
m_A=\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}f_A(x).
$$

**Shakan's stronger conjecture.** For every positive integer $S$, there exists $N_S\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that

$$
m_A\geq\frac{S}{3}
$$

for every $n\geq N_S$.

This strengthens the conjecture on arbitrarily large improvements for sum-free subsets by seeking the improvement through the maximum of the explicitly defined function $f_A$. Bourgain's earlier estimates answer the weaker conjecture for typical sets, while this stronger assertion remains open.
record.source_name: George Shakan, “On the largest sum-free subset problem in the integers”, arXiv:2207.14210 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14210

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Ramos's conjecture for the Grünbaum–Hadwiger–Ramos function
record.statement:
Let $\Delta(j,k)$ be the minimal dimension $d$ of a Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that every collection of $j$ masses in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits a $k$-arrangement equiparting all the masses. **Ramos's conjecture.**

$$
\Delta(j,k)=\left\lceil \frac{2^k-1}{k}j\right\rceil
$$

for every $j\geq 1$ and $k\geq 1$. The formula would determine the minimal dimension in the Grünbaum–Hadwiger–Ramos mass-partition problem. It is motivated by the lower bound derived from Avis's ideas and Ramos's work; the source presents the equality as a conjecture, with its general status unresolved.
record.source_name: Pavle V. M. Blagojević, Jaime Calles Loperena, Michael C. Crabb and Aleksandra S. Dimitrijević Blagojević, “Topology of the Grünbaum–Hadwiger–Ramos problem for mass assignments”, arXiv:2208.00666 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00666

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Minimum folded ribbonlength conjecture for Möbius-band unknots with linking number ±3
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}_{w,F}$ be a folded ribbon unknot that is a Möbius band, with ribbon linking number ${\operatorname{Lk}}(\mathcal{U}_{w,F})=\pm3$. Let ${\operatorname{Rib}}$ denote folded ribbonlength. **Minimum folded ribbonlength conjecture.** The minimum is

$$
{\operatorname{Rib}}([\mathcal{U}_{w,F}])=\inf_{\substack{\mathcal{U}_{w,F}\in\operatorname{Möbius},\\ {\operatorname{Lk}}(\mathcal{U}_{w,F})=\pm3}}{\operatorname{Rib}}(\mathcal{U}_{w,F})=3\sqrt{3}.
$$

The value is attained by the equilateral-triangle example established earlier for folded ribbon $3$-stick unknots. The conjecture asks whether allowing arbitrary Möbius-band folded ribbon unknots can lower this value.
record.source_name: Elizabeth Denne and Troy Larsen, “Linking number and folded ribbon unknots”, arXiv:2208.03239 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03239

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “This open problem is not the focus of this paper.”

record.title: Optimality conjecture for two-step lazy transposition shuffles
record.statement:
For $n\geq 2$, let $U_2(n)$ be the minimum number of transpositions in a $(2,n)$-shuffle, where a $(t,n)$-shuffle is a transposition shuffle whose transpositions have the specified parameter $t$. The paper reports that no $(2,n)$-shuffle using fewer than $2n-3$ transpositions is known.

**Optimality conjecture for $(2,n)$-shuffles.**

$$
U_2(n)=2n-3.
$$

This conjecture was previously made in the cited work on reachability and asserts that the observed lower bound is optimal for every $n\geq 2$. Its resolution is not supplied here.
record.source_name: Carla Groenland, Tom Johnston, Jamie Radcliffe and Alex Scott, “Perfect shuffling with fewer lazy transpositions”, arXiv:2208.06629 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06629

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “While we have given constructions which show that the upper bound for $U(n)$ can be improved by a constant factor, the new upper bounds are still a long way from the best known lower bound.”

record.title: Minimum length of 2-uniformity networks
record.statement:
A **2-uniformity network** is a network of lazy transpositions whose output permutation is uniformly distributed on every subset of two positions; let $U_2(n)$ denote the minimum length of such a network on $n$ positions. For $n\geq 2$, the conjecture is

$$
U_2(n)=2n-3.
$$

This is motivated by an explicit family of 2-uniformity networks of length $2n-3$; the conjecture asserts that no shorter sequences exist. Its status is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Carla Groenland, Tom Johnston, Jamie Radcliffe and Alex Scott, “Short reachability networks”, arXiv:2208.06630 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06630

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: The intersecting-family success-probability conjecture
record.statement:
Let $B=\{0,1\}^n$, and let $\mu$ be the uniform measure on $B^t$. An intersecting family is a set $W\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ such that for every $x,y\in W$ there is a coordinate $i$ with $x_i=y_i=1$. Let $p_{\mathrm{intersecting}}(t,n)$ be the maximum of $\mu(W)$ over $t$-tuples of intersecting families, and let

$$
p_{\mathrm{intersecting}}(t):=\lim_{n\to\infty}p_{\mathrm{intersecting}}(t,n).
$$

**Intersecting-family conjecture.** The success probability $p_{\mathrm{intersecting}}(t)$ tends to $0$ as $t$ grows.
This is stronger than the dictatorship version because every dictatorship is an intersecting family; the paper relates it to the normalized independence number of Hamming powers of Kneser graphs.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Ehud Friedgut, Gil Kalai and Guy Kindler, “The success probability in Levine's hat problem, and independent sets in graphs”, arXiv:2208.06858 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06858

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “We remark that Theorem settles the final open problem raised by Dong and Wu in .”

record.title: The Bollobás–Erdős–Tuza blocker conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $\alpha(G)$ be the size of a maximum independent set, and let $h(G)$ be the minimum cardinality of a vertex set intersecting every maximum independent set. **Bollobás–Erdős–Tuza blocker conjecture.** For every positive $\alpha$, if $\alpha(G)\geq\alpha n$, then $h(G)=o(n)$.
The conjecture concerns small hitting sets for maximum independent sets. The source states it as an earlier conjecture and discusses stronger proposed statements that fail in the exhibited examples; it does not report a resolution of this conjecture.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Ehud Friedgut, Gil Kalai and Guy Kindler, “The success probability in Levine's hat problem, and independent sets in graphs”, arXiv:2208.06858 (2023).

record.title: Minimum-order conjecture for odd and even D(k) graphs
record.statement:
Let $D^{odd}_{k,n}$ and $D^{even}_{k,n}$ denote the odd- and even-parity $D(k)$ graphs constructed in the paper, with order parameter $n$. 

**Minimum-order conjecture.** For all $k\geq 3$, there exists no $D^{odd}_{k,n}$ for all $n < 4k-3$ and $D^{even}_{k,n}$ for all $n < 3k$.

The authors construct such graphs for all $n\geq 4k-3$ in the odd case and all $n\geq 3k$ in the even case, and conjecture that these orders are minimal. The claim remains open.
record.source_name: David A. Kalarkop, Pawaton Kaemawichanurat and Raghavachar Rangarajan, “On graphs whose domination number is equal to chromatic and dominator chromatic numbers”, arXiv:2208.07020 (2022).

record.title: Bonichon and Morel's enumeration conjecture for 3-permutations avoiding $(12,12)$ and $(231,312)$
record.statement: A **3-permutation** is a permutation of three sequences, and avoidance of a tuple of patterns means that no componentwise occurrence of any listed pattern appears. Let $(12,12)$ and $(231,312)$ be the pairs of patterns to be avoided, and let $A295928$ denote the referenced OEIS sequence. **Bonichon and Morel's conjecture.** The number of 3-permutations avoiding the 3-patterns $(12,12)$ and $(231,312)$ is enumerated by the OEIS sequence $A295928$. The paper presents this as one of Bonichon and Morel's conjectures; it does not provide enough information here to determine whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Nathan Sun, “On d-permutations and Pattern Avoidance Classes”, arXiv:2208.08506 (2024).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08506

record.title: The fixed-diameter extremal tree conjecture for distance entropies
record.statement: Let $T$ be a tree of order $n$ and diameter $d\ll n$. Let $I_{f_s}(T)$ and $I_{f_e}(T)$ be the distance-based entropies associated with the functionals $f_s$ and $f_e$. **The fixed-diameter extremal tree conjecture.** The maximum values of $I_{f_s}$ and $I_{f_e}$ are attained by the tree obtained by identifying the central vertex of the star of order $n-d$ with a central vertex of the path of length $d$. The paper explains that this conjecture is false for general $I_{f_e}$, since the coefficients can be chosen so that an arbitrary preferred tree is extremal; it is true for $I_{ecc}$ in the relevant specialization.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie and Yanni Dong, “On the main distance-based entropies: the eccentricity- and Wiener-entropy”, arXiv:2208.12209 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12209

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2022). “Finally, Conjecture () is disproved.”

record.title: The self-similarity conjecture for extremal angle configurations
record.statement: A point configuration $\mathcal P$ is **self-similar** if there is a point $A\in\mathcal P$ such that every angle formed by three points of $\mathcal P$ can also be formed with $A$ as one of the points: for all $B,C,D\in\mathcal P$, there exist $E,F\in\mathcal P$ such that $\angle BCD=\angle AEF$ or $\angle BCD=\angle EAF$. **Self-similarity conjecture.** For $n$ sufficiently large, a configuration of $n$ points in general position with the smallest possible number of distinct angles exhibits self-similarity. The paper notes that self-similar configurations have at most $3\binom{n-1}{2}=O(n^2)$ distinct angles and presents constructions with this property, but does not establish that every extremal configuration has it.
record.source_name: Ruben Ascoli, Livia Betti, Jacob Lehmann Duke, Xuyan Liu, Wyatt Milgrim, Steven J. Miller, Eyvindur A. Palsson, Francisco Romero Acosta and Santiago Velazquez Iannuzzelli, “Distinct Angles and Angle Chains in Three Dimensions”, arXiv:2208.13284 (2023).

record.title: Upper-bound conjecture for disjoint perfect matchings in edge-connected r-graphs
record.statement:
For $0\leq t\leq r$, let $m(t,r)$ be the maximum integer $s$ such that every $t$-edge-connected $r$-graph has $s$ pairwise disjoint perfect matchings. **The upper-bound conjecture.** For all integers $l\geq 2$ and $r\geq 2l$, one has

$$
m(2l,r)\leq l-1.
$$

The paper has already proved the weaker upper bound $m(2l,r)\leq 3l-6$ for $l\geq 3$ and $r\geq 2l$; this conjecture would substantially sharpen it.
record.source_name: Yulai Ma, Davide Mattiolo, Eckhard Steffen and Isaak H. Wolf, “Edge-connectivity and pairwise disjoint perfect matchings in regular graphs”, arXiv:2208.14835 (2023).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2102.03720](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.03720), [arXiv:1503.05961](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.05961).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14835

record.title: Conjecture on super-maximized genera of graphs in surfaces
record.statement:
Let $V_c(g)$ be the maximum number of vertices of a graph of genus $g$ embedded in a surface, and let $b(g)$ be the stated upper bound for this quantity. For an integer $S$ satisfying $S\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 6$, set

$$
g=\frac{(S-1)(S-3)}{6}.
$$

**Super-maximization conjecture.** One has

$$
V_c(g)=b(g)
$$

whenever $g=\frac{(S-1)(S-3)}{6}\geq 4$ and $S\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 6$. This extends the theorem's verified infinite family of cases with $S\equiv 7\pmod {12}$, together with $S=9$, and asserts that all admissible genera in this parametrized family are super-maximized.
record.source_name: Dustin Connery-Grigg, François Lalonde and Jordan Payette, “Graphes dans les surfaces et ergodicité topologique”, arXiv:2209.00516 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00516

record.title: Minimum-volume conjecture for spherical knotoids
record.statement:
A **spherical knotoid** is a knotoid in $S^2$ whose associated hyperbolic complement has a hyperbolic volume. The knotoid $2_1$ denotes the spherical knotoid with the indicated two-crossing label.

**Minimum-volume conjecture.** The unique spherical knotoid of smallest volume is the knotoid $2_1$, and its volume is approximately $5.33349\dots$.

This conjecture identifies the smallest-volume spherical knotoid and gives a numerical estimate for its volume. The supplied text does not state whether the claim has been proved or disproved.

record.title: The maximal-index conjecture for klt Calabi-Yau varieties
record.statement:
Let $n\geq2$, let $X$ be the weighted Calabi-Yau hypersurface constructed in the source, and let $G$ be the cyclic subgroup acting freely in codimension one. Let $m=|G|$. **Maximal-index conjecture.** The quotient $X/G$ has index $m$, and in every dimension $n\geq2$ this is the largest possible index for a klt Calabi-Yau variety.

The first assertion depends on the conjectured faithfulness of the action on the canonical form; the source reports that the relevant calculation is verified computationally through dimension $30$. The stronger optimality assertion remains without a stated resolution.

record.title: Knor–Škrekovski–Tepeh conjecture on maximum-Wiener-index orientations of trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let $D$ be an orientation of $T$. The Wiener index $W(D)$ is the sum of the directed distances over all ordered pairs of vertices, where the distance is the length of a shortest directed path when one exists and is $0$ otherwise.

**Knor–Škrekovski–Tepeh conjecture.** If $D$ maximises $W(D)$ among all orientations of $T$, then there exists a vertex $v$ in $D$ such that for every vertex $u$ there exists either a $(u,v)$-path or a $(v,u)$-path in $D$.

The conjecture concerns the structure of orientations of trees with maximum Wiener index. The supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Fitting-index and group-order bounds in terms of character-table zeros
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $m(G)$ denote the maximum number of zeros in a row of the character table of $G$. Let $\mathbf F(G)$ denote the Fitting subgroup. **Fitting-index and group-order zero-bound conjecture.** The index $|G:\mathbf F(G)|$ is bounded in terms of $m(G)$. Furthermore, if $|\mathbf F(G)|$ is not abelian, then $|G|$ is bounded in terms of $m(G)$. The source notes that a bound for $|G:\mathbf F_8(G)|$ is known for arbitrary finite groups, but does not state that this conjecture is resolved.
record.source_name: Alexander Moretó, “Methods and questions in character degrees of finite groups”, arXiv:2209.09221 (2022).
